To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

transgenic tomato plants with the FeSOD gene under salinity show an increase in the number of chloroplasts in the cells, a decrease in the size and number of starch grains, an increase in the amount of starch, and a change in the size and shape (roundness) of the thylakoid membrane.

expression of the Arabidopsis thalina FeSOD1 in transgenic tomato regenerating plants under salt stress results in the decrease in the damage to ultrastructure of plastids and the mitochondria, and affects the size of their inclusions.

the transgenic tomato plants with the pea rbs gene leader sequence expressing FeSOD1 from Arabidopsis under salt stress have a higher level of chlorophyll, carotenoids, total protein, and proline than wild-type plants, and they also have a higher photosynthetic activity, a higher level of antioxidant activity, and a higher tolerance of salt stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the FeSOS1 gene as an effective genetic tool in improving salt tolerance of plants.
the study of the effect of salinity on the ultrastructural organization of organelles and their function in the cells of transgenic tomato lines expressing the gene FeSOD1 from Arabidopsis.
the study of the ultrastructural organization of the chloroplasts and mitochondrial apparatus of transgenic tomato expressing the FeSod1 gene from Arabi­dopsis thaliana under salinity conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transgenic plants with FeSOD1 from A. thaliana in the chloroplasts showed higher tolerance to salt stress than control plants.

the transgenic tomato plants with the FeSOD 1 gene from Arab. thaliana (FeSOD1) are tolerant to salinity and the tolerance is related to the increased activity of SOD and the accumulation of proline in leaves.
the transgenic plants expressing the Fe-dependent superoxide dismutase from Arabidopsis under the rbcS gene promoter have shown an enhanced resistance to salinity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the expression of the Fe-dependent superoxide dismutase (FeSOD) from Arabidopsis in the chloroplasts of transgenic tomato under saline conditions leads to a decrease of oxidative stress and the accumulation of the FeSod1 protein in the chloroplast stroma and in the thylakoid membrane, as well as the increase in the tolerance of transgenic plants to saline conditions.
the FeSOD transgenic tomato plants are more tolerant to salinity than the wild type.

the use of the FeSODY1 gene from Arabdopsis thaliana L. Heynh., with a pea rbcS promoter, in the transgenic tomato plants, leads to a reduction of damage in the ultrastructure organization of chloroplast and mitochondria and a change in the size and shape in their inclusions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transgenic tomato plants with the pea rbsC leader sequence showed a higher tolerance to salt stress than the wild-type control plants.
the expression of the Arabidopsis FeSOD1 transgene in tomato chloroplasts can be a promising strategy for increasing the resistance of crops to salt and drought stress.
transgenic tomato plants with the FeSOD gene under salinity have a higher tolerance to stress and are more productive than the control plants.
